# Dark Matter: Genesis - Unity 6 + URP Project Rules

You are an expert Unity 6 + URP C# developer building **Dark Matter: Genesis**, a light tactical RPG for PC and consoles (PS5 / Xbox) with WebGL/browser and mobile support as needed. Core features include survival lite RPG mechanics, crafting, exploration, melee combat (parry/combos/stamina/tension), moral choices, low to med poly Io mechanics, companion systems/animations/AI with formations and behavior, building materialization and destruction by elements and attacks, ranged combat (projectiles + inventory hotbar + mouse-aimed), and Pi Network integration.

**Core Principles**
- Prioritize WebGL/browser + mobile performance: object pooling, minimal Update() usage, efficient coroutines/events, lightweight physics/steering, profile frequently.
- Modular component-based architecture: MonoBehaviours for runtime behavior, ScriptableObjects for data/config (behaviors, items, recipes, combat stats, moral alignments, formations, etc.).
- Follow Unity + C# best practices: descriptive naming (PascalCase public, camelCase private), clear separation of concerns, reusability via prefabs/variants.
- Tactical light combat: responsive parry/combo windows, resource management (stamina/tension), positioning/flanking awareness.
- Cross-platform: Unity Input System, async patterns for Pi SDK, responsive/scalable UI.
- Reference existing repo files with @filename or relative paths for context.

**Key Systems to Align With**
- Central Stamina/Tension manager
- Inventory + hotbar system
- Melee state machine / Animator-driven combos + parry
- Moral choice event system
- Companion AI (formations, group behaviors, low-poly animations)
- Enemy AI (basic chase/attack/guard with light tactical positioning)
- Ranged projectile system with prefab projectiles and line tracers
- Building materialization / placement / Destruction
- Pi Network integration (browser-compatible)

**Enemy & Companion AI Guidelines**
- Enemies: Simple FSM for chase → attack. Light tactical elements (flanking, optimal range, aggro). Use NavMesh lightly or custom steering.
- Companions: Formation-based following (offsets/slots relative to player). Support roles in combat/exploration. ScriptableObject behaviors for variety.
- Shared: Efficient detection, events for interactions (e.g., player parry → companion opportunity), object pooling.

**Do’s**
- Use Unity built-in features wherever possible.
- Make behaviors configurable via ScriptableObjects.
- Add Gizmo/debug visuals for AI states, detection, and formations.
- Ensure all new code is WebGL + mobile friendly.
- Preserve and build on existing repo patterns.

**Don’ts**
- Avoid heavy dependencies, deep inheritance, or unprofiled performance hits.
- Do not invent unrelated systems. unless asked by user.
- Minimize polling; prefer events.

**Output Style**
- Clean, well-commented code with performance/tactical notes.
- Include Editor setup, prefab instructions, and test suggestions.
- Maintain consistency with the project’s architecture.
- when creating or updated systems, try to use the Invector systems and scripts

input.plan:
# PPT + name + HDRP on main

Cloud source of truth is already on origin:

- [Ppt entity management](bc-664e87b3-9282-440f-b270-3a5bf6957881) → `origin/cursor/ppt-directions-system-7881` (People/Places/Things directions MVP)
- [Hdrp project conversion](bc-76df442c-56b6-4be1-b954-65ad7ad180d1) → `origin/cursor/hdrp-migration-80d1` (scene rename + HDRP Phase 0/1 foundation)

PPT is **already based on current main** (`5fe4584b6`). HDRP is one commit behind (our identity commit) and will conflict in `ProjectSettings.asset`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ppt[ppt-directions-system-7881]
  hdrp[hdrp-migration-80d1]
  main[main]
  ppt -->|clean merge| main
  hdrp -->|resolve ProjectSettings| main
  main --> rename[SurvivalPioneer C# rename]
  rename --> unity[Unity HDRP Phase 0/1]
  unity --> mats["_Project material convert"]
  mats --> phase6["Phase 6 global switch later"]
```

## Guardrails before touching git

Working tree is heavily dirty (materials, docs, deleted `Pioneer v1.5.6.unity`). Playable scene on disk is already [`Assets/Dark Matter Genesis v1.56.unity`](Assets/Dark Matter Genesis v1.56.unity) and is the enabled build entry.

- Stash **unrelated** WIP; keep scene + `EditorBuildSettings` local rename.
- Stay on `main`. Merge **into** main (no checkout of cloud branches as the working copy).
- Keep ship title **Dark Matter: Genesis** in docs; keep `productName` as **Dark Matter Genesis** (no colon) to match the folder and last identity commit, unless Unity Player Settings already show the colon.
- Prefer the local scene path `Assets/Dark Matter Genesis v1.56.unity` over the cloud name `DarkMatter_Genesis v1.56.unity`.

## 1. Merge PPT onto main

Merge `origin/cursor/ppt-directions-system-7881`.

Adds the knowledge/directions layer (~33 files, +2200 lines):

- Runtime: [`PptManager`](Assets/_Project/Scripts/PPT/Runtime/PptManager.cs), resolver, keyword log, lime terrain tracer, NPC interactor/gestures
- Data: `PptEntry` / `PptNpcProfile` / `PptRegistry` ScriptableObjects
- UI: hold-E directions menu ([`PptDirectionsMenuUI`](Assets/_Project/Scripts/UI/PptDirectionsMenuUI.cs))
- Save: `GameSaveData.pptKnownKeywordIds` (save version 22)
- GameState: [`PptGameStateProvider`](Assets/_Project/Features/PPT/Adapters/PptGameStateProvider.cs)
- Design: [`PPT_System_Design.md`](Assets/_Project/Features/PPT/Documentation/PPT_System_Design.md)

After merge: wire `PptNpcInteractor` + `PptNpcGestureController` onto at least one existing quest-giver prefab (Hold E). Author a small `Resources/PPT/PptRegistry` starter set if the branch did not ship assets.

## 2. Merge HDRP foundation onto main

Merge `origin/cursor/hdrp-migration-80d1` (includes the scene-rename commit).

**Keep from HDRP branch**

- `com.unity.render-pipelines.high-definition` 17.4.0 in [`Packages/manifest.json`](Packages/manifest.json) (URP 17.4.0 stays until Phase 9)
- [`GenesisHdrpMigrationUtility.cs`](Assets/_Project/Editor/Rendering/GenesisHdrpMigrationUtility.cs) — Tools menus for Phase 0/1/6
- Five-tier graphics bootstrap + [`GraphicsCapabilityAdvisor`](Assets/_Project/Scripts/Core/GraphicsCapabilityAdvisor.cs)
- [`HDRP_Migration_Plan.md`](Assets/_Project/Documentation/Architecture/HDRP_Migration_Plan.md) and [`System_Requirements.md`](Assets/_Project/Documentation/System_Requirements.md)
- WebGL build-profile retirement
- Scene-path updates in [`.cursor/rules/confirm-before-depot-restore.mdc`](.cursor/rules/confirm-before-depot-restore.mdc)

**Resolve in our favor**

- [`ProjectSettings.asset`](ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset): keep `Dark Matter Interactive` / `Dark Matter Genesis`
- Scene file: keep `Assets/Dark Matter Genesis v1.56.unity` (already playable). Do not git-mv to underscored `DarkMatter_Genesis v1.56`. Patch HDRP docs/menus to that path.

Do **not** run Phase 6 (global Graphics pipeline switch) as part of the merge. That pinks the whole project.

## 3. C# name conversion (requested)

Mechanical rename with `git mv` so `.meta` GUIDs stay:

| Current | New |
|---|---|
| `SurvivalPioneerUiPalette` | `DarkMatterGenesisUiPalette` |
| `SurvivalPioneerEditorMenus` | `DarkMatterGenesisEditorMenus` |
| `SurvivalPioneerToolsWindow` | `DarkMatterGenesisToolsWindow` |

Update all `_Project` `.cs` references (palette is used in ~80 UI files; menus in most Editor tools). Update [`.cursor/rules/dark-matter-genesis-ui-palette.mdc`](.cursor/rules/dark-matter-genesis-ui-palette.mdc).

Out of scope unless you ask: `PioneerRoster*`, `PioneerCompanion*`, Invector package types.

## 4. Unity HDRP conversion (after compile)

Unity MCP is currently disconnected; this step needs the Editor open on `a:\Dark Matter Genesis`.

1. Wait for HDRP package import + compile (no console Errors).
2. Run **Tools / Dark Matter Genesis / HDRP / Phase 0/1 - Create Genesis HDRP Foundation** → `Assets/Settings/HDRP/Genesis_HDRP_{Performance,Balanced,Quality,High,Ultra}.asset`
3. Run **Phase 1 - Create HDRP Test Scene** → `Assets/_Project/Scenes/Genesis_HDRP_Test.unity`
4. Add a bulk URP→HDRP Lit converter under `Assets/_Project/Editor/Rendering/` and run it **only on `Assets/_Project`** first (not vendor packs).
5. Validate the test scene (lighting, volume, no pink ground). Leave [`Dark Matter Genesis v1.56.unity`](Assets/Dark Matter Genesis v1.56.unity) on URP until that looks right.
6. Phase 6 global switch + Gaia/Invector/Malbers pink audit is a **follow-up**, not this pass.

## What this pass will not finish

- ~1,600 vendor/third-party materials (Gaia, Invector, Malbers, VFX packs)
- Removing URP (Phase 9)
- Console 60 FPS cert / cinematic HDR tuning (Phases 7–8)
- Full PPT content authoring (all NPCs, keyword catalog)

## Commit / push

Three commits on `main` (then push if you confirm):

1. `feat: merge PPT directions system`
2. `feat: HDRP Phase 0/1 foundation and Genesis scene identity`
3. `refactor: rename SurvivalPioneer types to DarkMatterGenesis`

Do not include the unrelated dirty materials/docs stash in these commits.

# Hierarchy Sort Context Menu — Plan

Editor-only utility: right-click in Hierarchy → sort sibling GameObjects.

## Goal

Add a context menu on Hierarchy selection:

| Command | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| **Sort Children By Name** | Alphabetical (A→Z); optional reverse |
| **Sort Children By Age** | Creation / fileID order (older first) — see Age below |
| **Sort Children By Size** | Approximate world bounds volume / renderer bounds (largest first or smallest first) |

Scope: **children of the selected object(s)** (or selected siblings under a shared parent). Does not reparent across the scene.

## UX

- Context path: `GameObject/Dark Matter Genesis/Sort Children/...`
  - By Name (A→Z)
  - By Name (Z→A)
  - By Age (Oldest first)
  - By Age (Newest first)
  - By Size (Largest first)
  - By Size (Smallest first)
- Also mirror under `Tools/Dark Matter Genesis/Hierarchy/` via `DarkMatterGenesisEditorMenus` for discoverability.
- Multi-select: if several objects share one parent, sort those siblings only; if selection is a single parent, sort its direct children.
- Confirm dialog when child count > N (e.g. 100) to avoid accidental huge reorder.
- Full Undo: `Undo.SetTransformParent` is wrong here — use `Undo.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo` on the parent + `SetSiblingIndex` in a recorded undo group.

## Implementation

**New file:** `Assets/_Project/Editor/Hierarchy/HierarchySortUtility.cs`  
**Menu constants:** `DarkMatterGenesisEditorMenus.Hierarchy` + sort paths.

### Core API

```csharp
SortChildren(Transform parent, SortMode mode, bool ascending)
```

1. Collect `parent.GetChild(i)` into a list.
2. Sort with stable comparer for the mode.
3. Apply indices with `transform.SetSiblingIndex(i)` inside `Undo.IncrementCurrentGroup()` / `Undo.SetCurrentGroupName(...)`.
4. Mark scene dirty.

### Sort definitions

| Mode | Metric |
|------|--------|
| **Name** | `string.CompareOrdinal` / ignore-case culture-invariant on `gameObject.name` |
| **Age** | Prefer `LocalIdentifierInFile` / `Unsupported.GetLocalIdentifierInFile` for scene objects (lower ≈ older in file). Fallback: sibling index (current order) if ID unavailable. Prefab mode: local file ID within prefab. Document that “age” means **scene serialization age**, not wall-clock create time (Unity does not store create timestamps on GameObjects). |
| **Size** | For each child: encapsulate `Renderer.bounds` (and optionally `Collider.bounds`); use `extents` volume or max axis. Objects with no renderer/collider sort last (or treat as zero). Use world bounds so nested meshes count. |

### Validation

- `[MenuItem(..., true)]` validate: selection not empty; for “sort children”, selected transform has ≥ 2 children **or** ≥ 2 selected siblings.
- Disabled in Play Mode (or allow with warning — prefer Edit Mode only).
- Skip if parent is part of a locked prefab asset without unlocking (open Prefab Stage OK).

## Risks / notes

- Reordering can break scripts that assume sibling order (UI layout, waypoints). Undo mitigates; document in menu tooltip.
- “Age” is approximate (fileID), not true creation time — label menus clearly: “By Scene Age (file order)”.
- Size on empty parents / lights / empty transforms may be 0 — group them consistently.
- Do not sort across different parents in one operation.

## Out of scope (v1)

- Recursive sort of entire subtree
- Sort by component type / tag / layer
- Auto-sort on rename
- Project window asset sorting

## Test plan

1. Empty parent with 5 named cubes → Name A→Z / Z→A.
2. Create objects in order A then B then C → Age oldest-first matches creation order via fileID.
3. Large mesh vs small mesh under parent → Size largest-first.
4. Multi-select siblings → only those reorder.
5. Undo restores previous order.
6. Prefab Stage: sort children, apply, save.

## Effort

~1 small editor script + menu constants. Half hour to implement and smoke-test.

`protected` means only **that class and its subclasses** can read/write it.

**1. Add a public accessor on the camera (best for this project)**  
Since we already patch Invector’s camera for Pioneer zoom, expose it cleanly:

```csharp
public float CurrentZoom => currentZoom;
```

Then use `tpCamera.CurrentZoom` from `_Project` code. This is the fix already in progress.

`distance` is public, but it’s the **live** follow distance (can dip from wall culling).

**4. Change `protected` → `public` on Invector’s field (avoid)**  
Works, but makes upstream Invector harder to maintain/merge.

### Summary

We don’t “break” protection — we **expose what we need** via a public wrapper on the class we already own/patch. That’s the standard pattern for third-party code with `protected` internals.

## Review summary (camera / recoil / health HUD)

Overall the recent work is **sound for a single-player prototype**. Nothing looks like a ship-blocker, but there are a few **real bugs**, some **perf hotspots**, and **tuning risks** worth knowing.

---

### Bugs / correctness (fix when you can)

**1. Recoil offset never cleared on optics / weapon transitions**  
`ResetRecoilOffset()` exists but is **never called**. If you fire, then open binoculars or swap weapons mid-rebound, `offsetMouse` can still be non-zero when `tpCamera` re-enables → possible snap or tilt on exit.

**Advice:** Call `ResetRecoilOffset(tpCamera)` in `BeginBinocularCameraFreeze` and optionally on holster / reload cutscenes.

**2. Full-auto rebound velocity stacks without a cap**  
Each shot adds to `_recoilRecoveryVelocity` while also adding to `offsetMouse`. On high fire-rate weapons, velocity can **accumulate faster than the spring drains** → wobble or exaggerated dip on sustained fire.

**Advice:** Clamp `_recoilRecoveryVelocity` (e.g. pitch ±8°/s) or scale rebound down when `|velocity|` is already high.

**3. Spring integrator has no `deltaTime` clamp**  
A frame hitch (domain reload, stutter) can make the spring overshoot hard in one step.

**Advice:** Use `deltaTime = Mathf.Min(deltaTime, 1f/30f)` inside `TickRecoilRecovery`.

**4. Health bar still misses if `source == null`**  
`EnemyHealth.DamagedBy` only fires when `source != null`. Rare paths (environment, miswired projectile owner) won’t trigger `PushHealthHudImmediate()`.

**Advice:** Also listen to `HealthChanged` and show HUD when health drops while player is aiming at target, or ensure **every** player damage path passes the player root as `source`.

**5. `EnsureRuntimeZoomState` may fight intentional close zoom after aim**  
After releasing aim, if `currentZoom < preferred`, it **ForceSetZoomDistance(preferred)** every camera input frame until restored. That’s intended for scroll preservation, but if the player **deliberately** scrolls in closer after aiming, it may feel like zoom “snaps back out.”

**Advice:** Only restore preferred zoom **once** on aim→free-look transition, not every frame while `currentZoom < preferred`.

---

### Performance (fine now, watch at scale)

| Area | Issue | Impact |
|------|--------|--------|
| `PioneerShooterManager.LateUpdate` | Runs `SuppressInvectorNativeRecoil` + `ApplyShooterManagerDefaults` **every frame**, even when idle | Low–medium (redundant field writes on 3 weapons) |
| `EnemyHealthBarPresenter.LateUpdate` | **Every living enemy** with a presenter runs LateUpdate; engaged ones call `EnsureExists` + `ShowOrUpdate` every frame | Medium with many enemies in combat |
| `ResolveCanvasRoot()` | Uses `FindAnyObjectByType<UIManager>()` when HUD is first built / canvas moves | Low if cached; avoid calling per enemy per frame |
| `EnsureRuntimeZoomState` | Runs on **every** `CameraInput` while not in binoculars | Low (few struct writes) |
| Recoil spring tick | Runs every LateUpdate; early-outs when offset ≈ 0 | Negligible |

**Advice (priority order):**
1. Cache `UIManager` / canvas root on `EnemyHealthBarPresenter` in `Start` (static or singleton).
2. In `PioneerShooterManager.LateUpdate`, only run `SuppressInvectorNativeRecoil` when `isShooting` or weapon changed — not every idle frame.

The full-bar resets and unwanted target swaps came from the old priority system: every aggro enemy called `ShowOrUpdate` with `Time.time`, so whichever enemy ran `LateUpdate` last stole the bar — often showing a different enemy at **100% HP**.

### What changed

**Sticky engagement (`EngagedEnemyHealthHud`)**
- **`ShowFromPlayerDamage`** — only way to steal the bar from another enemy (player hit that target)
- **`UpdateFromEngagement`** — first enemy to aggro claims the bar; later aggro enemies are ignored while someone is already bound
- **`UpdateHealthIfBound`** — health updates only apply to the currently shown enemy (no cross-contamination)
- **`ReleaseEngagementCandidate`** — when an enemy de-aggroes before claiming the bar, it releases its slot

**Presenter tracking (`EnemyHealthBarPresenter`)**
- Records **`firstEngagedTime`** when engagement starts (false → true)
- Player damage still drives immediate HUD refresh via `ShowFromPlayerDamage`
- `HealthChanged` only updates the bar if this enemy is the bound target

### Expected behavior now
| Situation | Bar shows |
|-----------|-----------|
| Enemy A aggroes first, then B aggroes | **A** (sticky) |
| Player damages B while A is shown | **B** (player damage override) |
| Damage ticks on current target | Bar updates correctly, no reset to full |
| Second enemy aggroes alone | Cannot steal from first aggro target |
